question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following conditional probability density function:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}} & \,0<x\le 2,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{2}\,x \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(\frac{1}{4}<Y\,|\,X=\frac{3}{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$ 

In our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{4}<Y\,|\,X=\frac{3}{2}) & ={\int }_{1/4}^{3\sqrt{2}/2}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x=\frac{3}{2})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{3\sqrt{2}/2}\frac{y}{{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{4}{9}{\int }_{1/4}^{3\sqrt{2}/2}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{4}{9}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{1/4}^{3\sqrt{2}/2} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}({(\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}(\frac{9}{2}-\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}\cdot \frac{71}{16} \\  & =\frac{71}{72}.\end{aligned}
$$
